planting.note: Plant divisions or container-grown ferns in spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in light to full shade, sheltered from wind.

directions: Proliferum forms a soft, lacy, horizontally spreading clump of finely dissected evergreen fronds, a Divisilobum Group selection distinguished by small bulbils that form along the midrib of mature fronds, which can be pegged down onto moist compost to raise new plants without disturbing the parent. Site it in humus-rich, evenly moist, well-drained soil in light to full shade, sheltered from strong wind, where its dense horizontal frond display can be appreciated at close range along a path or in a shaded container. It is more heat-tolerant than many other Divisilobum selections and shows good resistance to verticillium wilt. Leave old fronds in place over winter to protect the crown, cutting back only tattered growth in early spring before new croziers unfurl.

planting.note: Plant divisions or container-grown plants in fall or early spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade.

directions: Geisha Girl is a selection of the Japanese woodland primrose producing flat, overlapping-petaled flowers in rich pink with a white eye and fine white tracing along the veins, carried in loose clusters above mid-green, softly textured foliage from April into May. Like other Japanese woodland primroses, the slowly creeping clumps go dormant and disappear completely by midsummer, so mark the spot or interplant with ferns and hostas to fill the summer gap. Grow in moist but well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial shade, dividing congested clumps just after flowering to maintain vigor and increase stock. This cultivar is known to sport readily, occasionally throwing shoots with different flower patterning on an established clump.

planting.note: Plant divisions or container-grown plants in spring in cool, moist, humus-rich, neutral to slightly acidic soil in partial shade.

directions: Marit was raised around 1980 by the Norwegian grower Marit Espejord from seed of a chance cross, and is generally regarded as the finest white-flowered form among the fertile perennial Himalayan poppy hybrids, producing clear white, silky-petaled flowers on tall stems above hairy, deeply cut foliage from late spring into summer. Grow it as you would its blue-flowered relatives, in cool, consistently moist, humus-rich soil enriched with leaf mold, in a site shaded from hot afternoon sun; it struggles in regions with hot, humid summers and performs best where summers stay cool. Deadhead spent flower stems to prolong bloom and prevent self-seeding of inferior offspring, and divide congested clumps in spring every few years to maintain vigor. Pair with hostas and ferns that share its preference for cool, moist shade.

planting.note: Plant divisions or container-grown plants in spring or fall in average, well-drained soil in partial shade to light sun.

directions: Bred in Germany, Herbstblüte (sometimes sold under the English trade name Autumn Glory) is valued for its unusually long bloom season among bergenias: light pink flower stalks open above the glossy, rounded, leathery leaves in spring and then rebloom sporadically through summer and into fall. The bold basal foliage takes on deep maroon-purple tones in cold weather, adding strong winter structure to the front of a shaded or partly shaded border. It is tough, drought-tolerant once established, and spreads gradually into a dense, weed-suppressing clump. Groom out tattered old leaves in early spring and divide crowded clumps every three to four years to keep flowering strong.

planting.note: Plant offsets or container-grown plants in spring in gritty, sharply drained, humus-rich soil in partial shade with protection from hot midday sun.

directions: An older, long-cultivated alpine-class show auricula, C.W. Needham carries dark purple-blue flowers with a small, lightly farina-dusted (meal-powdered) pale center, held above a neat rosette of serrated, farinose foliage. Grow in gritty, humus-rich, sharply drained soil and site where the farina-coated leaves stay dry overhead but the roots remain cool and evenly moist, such as a raised bed or trough in partial shade; overhead wet in winter can mark the mealy foliage and encourage rot. It is easiest to grow where summers are not excessively hot and humid. Divide and repot offsets every one to two years after flowering to keep the rosettes vigorous and true to form.

planting.note: Plant tubers in fall, 3-4 inches deep, in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade.

directions: This English selection emerges from dormant tubers in late September with glossy dark-green, arrow-shaped leaves marked by especially bold, bright silver-white veining that stands out against darker winter mulch and companion plantings. The foliage provides striking winter and early-spring interest in the shade garden, then dies back by late spring just before greenish-white, hooded spathe flowers appear, followed later by spikes of red berries. Like other Italian arums it goes fully dormant through summer, so interplant with later-emerging ferns or hostas to mask the gap. Leaf patterning varies somewhat from seed, so divide offset tubers in late summer to propagate true copies of this selection's especially heavy veining.

planting.note: Plant divisions or container-grown plants in spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade.

directions: Introduced in 2000 by Terra Nova Nurseries as a sport of 'Starry Eyes', Parisian Skies carries clear, evenly colored, bright true-blue forget-me-not-like flowers rather than the white-edged petals of its parent, held above a low mound of softly hairy, heart-shaped leaves from April into June. Grow in consistently moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade, where the carpet of foliage makes a fine groundcover beneath deciduous shrubs or at the front of a woodland border. It spreads gradually by short rhizomes without becoming invasive. Divide congested clumps after flowering to maintain vigor and increase stock, and provide a summer mulch to keep roots cool.

planting.note: Plant divisions or container-grown plants in spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade.

directions: Lilac Mist sets this navelwort selection apart with soft lavender-purple flowers rather than the typical sky-blue of the species, held in loose sprays above a low, spreading mound of hairy, heart-shaped leaves in spring. Grow in evenly moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade, where it forms an effective, slowly spreading groundcover at the front of a woodland border or beneath deciduous shrubs. It benefits from a summer mulch to keep roots cool and combines well with hellebores, ferns, and spring-flowering woodland bulbs. Divide clumps after flowering every few years to maintain vigor and propagate true to the soft lilac color.
